bibliographic.title: Safety-focused development and evaluation of an LLM sexual well-being chatbot for women: A methods-focused feasibility study
bibliographic.authors: Alice E McGee, Guy Parsons, Liudmila Zhaunova, Alison Paul, Aliaksandr Kazlou, Yihan Xu, Heorhi Stsefanovich, Anna Klepchukova, András Meczner
bibliographic.citation_apa: McGee, A. E., Parsons, G., Zhaunova, L., Paul, A., Kazlou, A., Xu, Y., Stsefanovich, H., Klepchukova, A., & Meczner, A. (2026). Safety-focused development and evaluation of an LLM sexual well-being chatbot for women: A methods-focused feasibility study. unclear. https://doi.org/10.1177/20552076261435861

methodology.method_family: methods-focused feasibility study with multi-stage development and evaluation
methodology.study_design: interdisciplinary medically led three-phase development process with five-stage evaluation framework combining synthetic test cases, clinician-led vulnerability testing, and controlled release to real users
methodology.sample_description: controlled release to real users of an LLM-based sexual well-being chatbot in a mobile application
methodology.sample_size: 5195 real user interactions reviewed in controlled release
methodology.technology_context: LLM-based educational chatbot named Expert with auxiliary LLM Critic for semi-automated evaluation and clinician review in a mobile application

eligibility.decision_rationale: The article directly designs and evaluates a safety-focused framework for an LLM conversational agent in a sensitive healthcare domain, reporting staged governance mechanisms including clinician oversight, vulnerability testing, risk governance, and monitoring of real-user dialogues at scale.
eligibility.manual_spotcheck_reason: Only front matter and partial methods text were provided; full methods, ethics, governance implementation details, and limitations sections were not available for complete appraisal.

appraisal.notes: Clear feasibility objective and staged evaluation with predefined thresholds and quantified safety outcomes. Ethics and fuller methodological detail are not visible in the supplied excerpt.

cerqual.explanation: Findings are coherent and quantitatively reported for a feasibility study in a regulated health context, but appraisal is limited by incomplete full text and limited visibility of ethics, governance operations, and long-term monitoring design.

coding.theme: Safety-focused governance framework for LLM conversational health systems
coding.subtheme: Staged clinical oversight and automated critic-assisted review in sexual well-being chatbots
rq_alignment: governança de IA generativa em sistemas conversacionais

synthesis.main_claim: A structured, medically led framework can feasibly develop and evaluate an LLM sexual well-being chatbot with clinical safety oversight, meeting predefined accuracy and safety thresholds across synthetic, clinician-led, and real-user stages.
synthesis.contribution: Provides an end-to-end safety-focused development and evaluation framework, including Expert-Critic architecture and five-stage assessment, with reported error and unsafe-response rates in a controlled real-user release.
synthesis.limitations: Supplied text notes manual review limits at scale and positions the work as feasibility-focused; broader governance, compliance, auditability, and long-term operational learning details are not evidenced in the excerpt.
synthesis.use_in_review: Use as central empirical evidence on conversational governance mechanisms for regulated LLM health chatbots, especially staged human oversight, vulnerability testing, critic-assisted flagging, and post-release dialogue review.

evidence.claim: Study uses a specific LLM-based conversational chatbot in a regulated health context.
evidence.excerpt: This study designed and evaluated a safety-focused framework for an LLM-based sexual well-being chatbot in a mobile application.

evidence.claim: Research design is a methods-focused feasibility study with staged evaluation.
evidence.excerpt: We conducted a methods-focused feasibility study comprising a multi-stage development and evaluation of the chatbot.

evidence.claim: Evaluation combines synthetic cases, clinician vulnerability testing, and real-user controlled release.
evidence.excerpt: a five-stage evaluation framework combining synthetic test cases, clinician-led vulnerability testing and controlled release to real users

evidence.claim: Real-user sample size and monitored dialogue count are reported.
evidence.excerpt: In a controlled release, 5195 real user interactions were reviewed.

evidence.claim: Predefined safety/accuracy outcomes were met with low clinically inaccurate and unsafe responses.
evidence.excerpt: Clinically inaccurate responses occurred in 0.90% (47/5195) of dialogues, with unsafe responses within severity thresholds.

evidence.claim: Clinical safety and risk governance are central design outcomes.
evidence.excerpt: our approach positions clinical safety and risk governance as central design and evaluation outcomes.

evidence.claim: Governance includes translating safety principles into design requirements and safeguards.
evidence.excerpt: translating high-level safety principles into explicit design requirements and implementing technical and content safeguards during chatbot development.

evidence.claim: Human-in-the-loop oversight is implemented via clinician review supported by an auxiliary Critic LLM.
evidence.excerpt: we also incorporated a second LLM as an auxiliary 'Critic' to support semi-automated evaluation by flagging potentially problematic responses for clinician review.

evidence.claim: Article explicitly frames human-in-the-loop and risk assessment as core topics.
evidence.excerpt: Keywords Large language models, digital health, chatbots, human-in-the-loop AI, risk assessment, clinical safety

evidence.claim: Framework is presented as transferable to other sensitive clinical domains.
evidence.excerpt: This approach helps to address gaps in safety reporting and could be adapted for other sensitive clinical domains.

evidence.claim: Peer review status is indicated by submission and acceptance dates.
